summary: 30-ft wooden lookout built July 1910 on Fort Noble Mountain, replaced 1916 by a 50-ft steel tower; closed 1978 and later removed; no source describes the site today.

corrections.proposed: Forest, Fish and Game Commission (1910); Conservation Commission (from 1916)
corrections.why: The record's agency holds a date fragment copied from the Eastern site's 1910 entry. Wikipedia names the commission that built the 1910 tower and the one that replaced it in 1916.
9.1 m (30 ft) is the height of the 1910 wooden tower. Wikipedia says the 1916 replacement was 50 ft (15 m) of steel, and that is the tower that stood when the lookout closed in 1978.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 30-foot (9.1 m) figure describes the 1910 wooden tower; the 50-foot (15 m) figure describes the steel tower that replaced it in 1916. Both are correct for different towers.

Wikipedia dates wooden steps added inside the tower to 1918 or 1919; the Eastern site dates a self-supporting stairway that replaced the outside ladder to 1930. These may be two different changes. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Built July 1910, the 1916 replacement, the 1978 end of lookout work and the record's Herkimer/Hamilton location come from Wikipedia and agree with the Eastern site where the two overlap. The Eastern site's 1945 observer item is the only staffing evidence. The removal date is not in any source we could read: a Facebook group post in search results gives 1985 (with closure in 1978), but the post could not be read through the cache, so it is not used. Wikipedia gives elevation 2,310 ft, while CNY Hiking gives 2338 ft; not used. The 'July 1910:' agency value in the record is a parsing error and is corrected. The height correction (9.1 m to 15 m) assumes the record describes the tower standing at closure; the editor may prefer to show both heights. No photos found with usable image URLs. The Eastern site says the 1945 observer item is from the Adirondack Record-Elizabethtown Post; the story does not repeat the porcupine anecdote.
